name: Marcus Tan
profile_summary: Marcus Tan is a driven, analytical Singapore-based CEO, managing technology and logistics teams across multiple Asia-Pacific hubs. With frequent travel and complex coordination demands, he values data-driven, low-friction routines designed to improve metabolic health, maintain functional strength, and optimize energy and sleep on the road—with minimal decision fatigue.

monday_to_friday.notes: In-office core hours; occasional late investor or cross-region calls until 21:00.

saturday.notes: Catch-up strategy, light work, or personal training/recovery.

sunday.notes: Reserved for family, meal planning, chef prep, and recovery.

goals.name: Improve metabolic health
goals.description: Reduce metabolic risk with structured meals, aerobic conditioning, measured protein, and regular physician and lab review.

goal_targets.notes: Breakfast, lunch, and dinner structure and aerobic conditioning each count directly; supplement, meal planning, and chef prep are support-only.

goals.name: Build and maintain safe, lean strength
goals.description: Build strength, especially lower-body and core, without aggravating right-knee or lower-back issues.
success_indicators: trainer or physio assessment after travel

goal_targets.notes: Knee-modified strength or trainer-led sessions count. Mobility or assessment are support-only unless they replace strength after travel or pain.

goals.name: Preserve energy and consistent sleep, especially around travel
goals.description: Protect sleep duration and quality, especially on high-stress travel or late-call weeks, by targeting recovery, adjusting activity, and using provider support.
success_indicators: Less dropoff in sleep on travel

goal_targets.notes: Stretching, mobility, tailored post-travel routines, and sleep hygiene actions count. Logging or reminders are support-only.

goals.name: Improve adherence and enable reliable preventive care
goals.description: Reduce fall-off during heavy travel weeks, ensure timely labs, and improve care-team coordination without increasing friction.
success_indicators: Follow up on scheduled labs and reviews
Physician and dietitian reviews completed after screenings

goal_targets.notes: Labs and provider review count in due weeks only; adherence tasks and supplement protocols are tracked but don't inflate core coverage.
Full-horizon target used for 3-month goal attainment review.

goals.name: Maintain healthspan routines during heavy travel
goals.description: Adapt core meal, movement, and provider routines while traveling. Accept substitutions as needed, prioritize continuity and quick recovery post-travel.
success_indicators: 1+ physical activity session completed during each travel window
Structured meal adherence 80%+ during travel weeks
At least 2 recovery/mobility sessions per multi-day trip

goal_targets.notes: Travel is tracked as adaptation context. Travel meals, training, recovery, and remote care count toward their underlying weekly actions; this goal watches continuity and substitution quality without adding a separate core denominator.
Full-horizon target used for 3-month goal attainment review.

training_preferences: prefers trainer-led and data-driven strength progressions
needs knee-safe modifications for certain exercises
accepts remote or app-based coaching during travel
dislikes purely treadmill or monotonous cardio
nutrition_preferences: values practical meal solutions over restrictive tracking
enjoys Singaporean, Japanese, Mediterranean, Indian, and Vietnamese cuisine
willing to cook/assemble at home up to 2x per week; prefers chef or no-prep otherwise
does not want strict calorie counting
consultation_preferences: prefers in-person physio and movement review when available

dietary_access_plan.office_meal_access: chef-prepped packed lunch or office delivery during work blocks

normal_week_strategy.breakfast: home chef-prepped or low-prep high-protein breakfast
normal_week_strategy.lunch: structured office lunch from chef-prepped packed meal or office delivery
normal_week_strategy.dinner: home chef-prepped meal, with limited structured restaurant dinners when work or social context requires

travel_meal_strategy.planned_high_resource_travel: hotel buffet or room-service breakfast; restaurant or hotel lunch and dinner with dietitian guidance when needed
travel_meal_strategy.last_minute_low_resource_travel: restaurant or room-service meals, fewer assumptions about ideal structure, remote dietitian support if adherence risk rises

dietary_access_plan.notes: Chef/provider work should appear as food-source context unless Marcus actively participates. Office lunch should be schedulable while Marcus is at the office.

physical.name: Mild right-knee irritation
physical.description: Mild irritation post running or high flexion, aggravated if volume increases abruptly.
implications: use cycling, rowing, or swimming during flare-ups

physical.name: Lower-back tightness after >3h flight or long sitting
physical.description: Back tightness emerges often after flights exceeding 3 hours or long conference days.
implications: avoid heavy deadlifts or loaded movements immediately after flights

schedule: occasional last-minute trips to Jakarta or Bangkok (short notice)
client dinners up to 3x per month
behavioral: adherence drops if routines are overly complex or require daily meal prep/logging
low friction is essential for routines to persist during travel
opposes wellness interventions without clear, quantified rationale
medical_safety: abnormal or trend-worsening labs route to physician review
high-intensity or high-load activity avoided after fatigue, travel, or pain

sleep.main_issue: work-travel rhythm, investor calls, and late client dinners

journey_phases.trigger: Start of new HealthSpan plan. Initial labs, chef briefing, and movement review.
scheduling_biases: prioritize baseline labs and movement review
avoid sudden increases in lower-body load
use in-person chef and trainer when possible

journey_phases.trigger: Planned board meetings in Hong Kong. Use hotel gym and remote consults.
scheduling_biases: prioritize aerobic and basic resistance training using hotel equipment
use quick meal check-ins, chef-prepped or no-prep options
avoid lab scheduling; all reviews remote

journey_phases.trigger: Return from travel, stabilize routines and monitor metrics.
scheduling_biases: reaffirm morning sessions, check-in with dietitian
progress strength work gradually
confirm post-travel sleep/adherence

journey_phases.trigger: Planned Tokyo board and investor travel; full week out of Singapore, limited gym.
scheduling_biases: accept hotel gym or bodyweight subs
use remote coach/dietitian as needed
schedule mobility after arrival

journey_phases.trigger: Synthetic mild knee and back flare after post-travel overload.
scheduling_biases: substitute strength with mobility; schedule physio consult
minimize high load lower-body training
coordinate handoff for trainer and physiotherapist

journey_phases.trigger: Last-minute Jakarta escalation: low-resource, high stress, remote-only support.
scheduling_biases: focus on travel-compatible exercises
structured eating mostly by restaurant with check-ins
log fatigue post-travel

journey_phases.trigger: End-of-quarter check, final progress review, and next cycle planning.
scheduling_biases: complete provider reviews/labs as due
plan travel mitigation for next cycle
avoid last-minute overload

ordinary_weekday_pattern.notes: Preferred for home training, remote fitness or nutrition consultation, or chef breakfast.
Work focus; only short, low-complexity tasks feasible.
Backup evening training window. Sometimes gym or travel-screen.
Recovery, low-load habits, and wind down. Avoid strenuous sessions.

weekend_pattern.notes: Longer training with trainer or physiotherapist, or chef prep.
Family, meal planning, chef prep, and light movement.

limitations: no in-person trusted physio or lab
some jetlag from travel over 3 hours
travel_windows.notes: Planned high-resource travel. Hotel gym and pool available; care coordination shifts mostly remote except chef-prepped meals.
Moderate-resource travel. Meals partly chef-prepped, most fitness sessions require adaptation.

limitations: no chef or trusted local providers
increased work stress and energy drop
travel_windows.notes: Low-resource travel, mainly supports travel-compatible movement and remote check-ins. Designed to force substitutions and unscheduled support tasks.

goal_actions.label: Complete structured metabolic meals
goal_actions.notes: Chef-prepped, member-assembled (<2x per week), or travel-compatible meals count as structured. Supplement protocols or meal planning do not count.

goal_actions.label: Complete aerobic conditioning
goal_actions.notes: Zone 2 ‘true cardio’, swimming, cycling, or suitable travel/hotel-gym equivalents count directly.

goal_actions.label: Complete knee-modified strength sessions
goal_actions.notes: Trainer-led, hotel-gym, or bodyweight alternatives count if following knee-safe plan. Mobility substituted only post-travel or pain.

goal_actions.label: Complete sleep and fatigue recovery actions
goal_actions.notes: Evening mobility, recovery, post-flight stretching, and travel sleep protection actions count. Logging or reminders do not.

goal_actions.label: Complete preventive lab or provider review (when due)
goal_actions.notes: Only counts on scheduled lab, physician, or dietitian review weeks. Remote or in-person review is valid.

goal_actions.label: Complete support adherence or supplement protocol
goal_actions.notes: Daily supplements, check-in logging, and checklist review support adherence but do not count as core outcome progress.

goal_actions.label: Complete care-team review and decision follow-through
goal_actions.notes: Counts physician, dietitian, physio, remote care-team handoff, plan-adjustment review, and lab-result follow-up touchpoints. Passive logs and reminders do not count.

goal_actions.label: Complete behavior coaching and friction-resolution touchpoints
goal_actions.notes: Counts member-facing coaching, adherence barrier review, travel friction planning, post-missed-session coaching, and meal-prep failure resolution. Daily supplement-taking does not count.
